_design_note: Neutral policy and update descriptions. No raw convergence scores or tensor delta norms in candidate texts. PSE tags (boundary_violation, keep_tensor_unchanged, require_recompute, reject_candidate, valid_coupling_update, invariant1_violation, dissolution_grundsatz, handoff_violation, determinism_violation, wrong_policy) are the only reliable signal. Name-trap 1: KeepTensorUnchanged and RequireRecompute are real StitchFailurePolicy variants but map to G_delta and G_trace failures respectively — BoundaryViolation takes priority when g_boundary fails. Name-trap 2: dissolution_clears_trace sounds like valid maintenance but violates the Dissolution-Grundsatz (trace/evidence/gate-history must be preserved); handoff_finalizes_externally sounds like a legitimate completion step but the spec says Handoff produces only candidates, never external commit artefacts.

cases.title: StitcherGate: G_boundary, G_delta, and G_trace all fail — which failure policy is emitted?

phase_matrix_context.description: StitcherGateReport with g_boundary=false, g_delta=false, g_trace=false (all other sub-gates pass). The StitcherGate evaluation applies failure policies in strict priority order: (1) !g_boundary -> BoundaryViolation; (2) !g_delta -> KeepTensorUnchanged; (3) !g_trace -> RequireRecompute; (4) else -> RejectCandidate. BoundaryViolation is always selected when g_boundary fails, regardless of how many other gates also failed. The matrix-boundary seam violation is the hardest category — it means the candidate crossed a declared boundary constraint, not merely a metric threshold.

Removes the candidate from the active stitch pool and re-evaluates the ResonanceFabricState to identify which cluster formation triggered the seam-crossing. Routes corrected candidates within declared boundary constraints.

Failure policy that keeps the FieldTensorState byte-identical to its pre-evaluation state. Emitted when the tensor-delta norm sub-gate fails, indicating the proposed delta exceeds the permitted magnitude.
candidates._trap: KeepTensorUnchanged applies to G_delta failure (priority branch 2). G_boundary failure triggers BoundaryViolation at branch 1 before G_delta is checked.

candidates.text: Failure policy that forces a full recompute of Fabric-H before the candidate is retried. Emitted when the trace is not ready (trace hash is zero or trace is absent).
candidates._trap: RequireRecompute applies to G_trace failure (priority branch 3). G_boundary failure at branch 1 takes precedence.

candidates.text: Failure policy that permanently discards the candidate from the stitch pool. Emitted as the fallback when no higher-priority failure condition matches.
candidates._trap: RejectCandidate is the fallback (branch 4). G_boundary failure triggers BoundaryViolation at branch 1 — RejectCandidate is never reached when g_boundary fails.

Applies the candidate's proposed delta directly to the FieldTensorState, bypassing the StitcherGate check for the delta and boundary sub-gates.
Advances the stitch candidate to the Handoff stage without waiting for a passing StitcherGateReport, treating the boundary seam violation as a non-blocking warning.

cases.title: Fabric-H → Fabric-T gate audit — which CouplingUpdates have a valid path to FieldTensorState?

phase_matrix_context.invariant1_rule: Fabric-H events MUST NOT mutate Fabric-T directly. Fabric-T may only change via an accepted CouplingUpdate that references a passed StitcherGateReport. Dissolution must preserve trace, evidence and gate history (Dissolution-Grundsatz).
phase_matrix_context.description: Eight proposed operations were submitted for Fabric-H to Fabric-T path audit. Invariant 1 requires that FieldTensorState only changes via CouplingUpdate[] that references a StitcherGateReport with passed=true. A CouplingUpdate without any StitcherGateReport reference is an Invariant 1 violation. A CouplingUpdate that references a StitcherGateReport with passed=false is also invalid. Direct mutations from ResonanceFabricState to FieldTensorState bypass the gate entirely. Dissolution that removes trace entries violates the Dissolution-Grundsatz. Handoff may produce candidate references but never creates external commit artefacts.

CouplingUpdate for a mirror-consistent stitch candidate. The update references a passed StitcherGateReport. Gate checks for convergence, mirror-consistency, delta, budget, trace, boundary and evidence all succeeded.
CouplingUpdate for a boundary-aligned cluster candidate. Carries a StitcherGateReport reference where passed=true. Tensor delta norm is within the configured threshold.

CouplingUpdate for a high-convergence candidate produced during a MorphodynamicField event. The update carries no StitcherGateReport reference — it was generated directly from the Fabric-H event output.
candidates._trap: No StitcherGateReport reference. Invariant 1 requires every Fabric-T update to reference a passed gate report. High convergence does not bypass this requirement.

candidates.text: CouplingUpdate that references a StitcherGateReport for this candidate. The gate report records passed=false with failure_policy=RejectCandidate.
candidates._trap: Referencing a StitcherGateReport is necessary but not sufficient — the referenced report must have passed=true. This update references a failed gate, violating Invariant 1.

candidates.text: ResonanceFabricState event that writes updated field coordinates directly to FieldTensorState, skipping the StitcherGate evaluation entirely for this resonance pulse.
candidates._trap: Fabric-H events MUST NOT mutate Fabric-T directly (Invariant 1). This is a direct violation regardless of the magnitude of the resonance pulse.

candidates.text: Dissolution operation that compacts the working ResonanceFabricState by removing superseded trace entries and clearing the gate history to reduce memory footprint.
candidates._trap: Dissolution may compact working state but MUST preserve trace, evidence and gate history (Dissolution-Grundsatz). Clearing trace entries is a spec violation even if the intention is compaction.

candidates.text: Handoff operation that advances a cluster candidate and creates a finalised external commit artefact in the downstream PSE-Bridge, recording the candidate as an accepted crystal.
candidates._trap: Handoff produces only candidates; it NEVER creates external commit or finalisation artefacts. PSE-Bridge is the only crystal-commit path.

candidates.text: Applies a CouplingUpdate directly when the cluster's urgency score exceeds a configured threshold, bypassing G_boundary and G_evidence sub-gate checks for time-critical updates.
CouplingUpdate that carries a modified timestamp placing the update in a previous cycle, and references the StitcherGateReport from that earlier cycle as its gate proof.
candidates._trap: Using a gate report from a different cycle as proof for the current update violates the determinism invariant. Every update must reference the StitcherGateReport from its own evaluation cycle.

resonance_fabric_direct_write (direct Fabric-H to Fabric-T mutation — Invariant 1)

cases.title: CouplingUpdate cycle audit — which updates carry a StitcherGateReport from the correct evaluation cycle (cycle N)?

phase_matrix_context.determinism_invariant: Every CouplingUpdate must reference a StitcherGateReport that was issued in the same evaluation cycle as the update itself (cycle N). A gate report from a prior cycle (N-1 or earlier) may carry passed=true but it is not valid proof for a current-cycle update. Using a prior-cycle report as the gate reference produces a DeterminismViolation because the update cannot be deterministically replayed against the current cycle's gate state.
phase_matrix_context.description: A batch of eight CouplingUpdates is under audit for Fabric-H to Fabric-T path validity. Each update must satisfy two conditions: (1) it carries a StitcherGateReport reference with passed=true, AND (2) that StitcherGateReport was issued in the current evaluation cycle (cycle N). Updates that reference a passed report from cycle N-1 or N-2 fail the determinism invariant even though their gate report shows passed=true. Updates with no gate reference are Invariant 1 violations. Updates that directly mutate Fabric-T bypass the gate path entirely.

candidates.text: CouplingUpdate for a convergent cluster candidate. References StitcherGateReport gate_alpha issued in the current evaluation cycle (cycle N). Report records passed=true. All sub-gates passed in this cycle.

CouplingUpdate for a mirror-consistent stitch candidate. References StitcherGateReport gate_beta issued in cycle N. The report's passed field is true; all sub-gate checks (convergence, mirror, delta, boundary, evidence) completed in the current cycle.
CouplingUpdate for a boundary-aligned candidate. StitcherGateReport gate_gamma was issued in cycle N with passed=true. Tensor delta norm within configured threshold, evaluated in this cycle.

CouplingUpdate for a high-convergence candidate. References StitcherGateReport gate_delta from cycle N-1, where passed=true. The candidate was re-queued from the previous cycle and its prior gate result is being reused as proof.
candidates._trap: The gate report carries passed=true, but it was issued in cycle N-1. The determinism invariant requires the StitcherGateReport to be from the same evaluation cycle as the update. Reusing a prior-cycle passed report is a DeterminismViolation.

candidates.text: CouplingUpdate for a drift-stabilizing candidate. The referenced StitcherGateReport gate_epsilon has passed=true and all sub-gates satisfied, but the report was generated in cycle N-1 during a preliminary evaluation pass.
candidates._trap: A prior-cycle gate report, even with passed=true and all sub-gates satisfied, does not provide valid same-cycle proof. The current cycle may have different Fabric-H state, making the prior report non-deterministic as a proof for cycle N.

candidates.text: CouplingUpdate that reuses StitcherGateReport gate_zeta from cycle N-2. The report is marked passed=true and was generated for the same candidate hash during an earlier evaluation window.
candidates._trap: Cycle N-2 gate report reuse. The staleness is even greater than N-1. The determinism invariant applies regardless of how distant the prior cycle is — any cross-cycle gate reference is a violation.

candidates.text: CouplingUpdate for a resonance-triggered candidate. The update carries no StitcherGateReport reference — it was emitted directly from the MorphodynamicField event without gate evaluation.
candidates._trap: No gate reference at all. Invariant 1 requires every Fabric-T update to reference a passed gate report from the current cycle. Missing reference is an Invariant 1 violation distinct from the cycle-mismatch determinism violation.

candidates.text: ResonanceFabricState event that writes updated field coordinates directly to FieldTensorState during cycle N, skipping the StitcherGate evaluation entirely for this resonance pulse.
candidates._trap: Direct Fabric-H to Fabric-T mutation. Invariant 1 prohibits this regardless of which cycle the event occurs in.
